title: Regular Expressions for Glycan Structures
text: glymotif provides concise syntax matching glycan motifs. However, exact motif matching may sufficient express complex structural constraints. example, sialyl-LacNAc motif without fucosylation specified using bare IUPAC-condensed sequence. address limitation, glyrex introduces dedicated glyco-regex syntax enables flexible expressive pattern matching.

title: Regular Expressions for Glycan Structures
code: library(glyrex) x <- c(   "Gal(b1-4)[Fuc(a1-3)]GlcNAc(a1-",   "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-",   NA_character_ ) p <- rex_compile("Galb4-(Fuca3-)GlcNAc") rex_detect(x, p) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA rex_extract(x, p) #> [1] "Fuc(a1-3)[Gal(b1-4)]GlcNAc(a1-" NA #> [3] NA rex_match(x, "(?<antenna>Galb4)-GlcNAc") #>      match                 antenna #> [1,] "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(a1-" "Gal(b1-" #> [2,] "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-" "Gal(b1-" #> [3,] NA                    NA rex_locate_all(x, p) #> [[1]] #>     nodes edges #> 1 1, 2, 3  1, 2 #> #> [[2]] #> [1] nodes edges #> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names) #> #> [[3]] #>   nodes edges #> 1    NA    NA

title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: pattern describes connected residues glycan graph. Read path left right, towards reducing end. Separate adjacent residues -: example, Gal-GlcNAc asks Gal attached directly GlcNAc. skip intervening residues. Without end anchors, path can occur within larger glycan describe whole structure. Start residue names, add constraints needed: Gal matches galactose residue. . matches one residue, number residues. Hex HexNAc match members corresponding glyrepr classes; example, Hex matches Gal, Glc, Man. Sia matches Neu5Ac, Neu5Gc, Kdn. [Gal|Man] matches either Gal Man. Alternatives can also paths, [Gal-GlcNAc|Gal-GalNAc]. [^Fuc] matches one residue Fuc. Negated alternatives must describe single residue; [^Fuc|Xyl] excludes Fuc Xyl.

what: Specifying linkages and the reducing end
title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: linkage belongs residue non-reducing side. example, Galb4-GlcNAc requires Gal attached GlcNAc beta1-4 linkage. Use glyco-regex linkage suffixes Galb4; IUPAC-style linkages Gal(b1-4) supported patterns. suffix specifies anomer acceptor position. donor position 1, 2 Neu5Ac, Neu5Gc, Kdn, Sia. Omitted linkage fields impose constraint. Thus Gal-GlcNAc specify linkage, GlcNAca specifies alpha anomer, either internal residue reducing end. specified acceptor position, GlcNAca4, requires outgoing glycosidic linkage towards reducing end match reducing-end residue . require reducing-end GlcNAc alpha anomer, use GlcNAca$. Unknown linkage fields (?) act wildcards either pattern input glycan, following glycowork. specified linkage can therefore match input whose corresponding field unknown; match establishes compatibility, certainty linkage. Ambiguous positions match possible values overlap, acceptor 3/4 compatible 4 6.

title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: Ordinary parentheses describe sibling branch attached next residue main path. attachment dash must inside parentheses, dash branch group. Galb4-(Fuca3-)GlcNAc, Gal Fuc attach GlcNAc: Gal beta1-4 Fuc alpha1-3. Fuc inserted Gal GlcNAc. Required branch residues part match. Additional branches allowed unless explicitly excluded. Pattern parentheses serve different purpose square brackets used branches input IUPAC string Gal(b1-4)[Fuc(a1-3)]GlcNAc. Use (!...-) require absence sibling branch. example, Galb4-(!Fuc-)GlcNAc matches Gal-GlcNAc path GlcNAc remaining Fuc branch linkage. Galb4-(!Fuca3-)GlcNAc excludes branch compatible alpha1-3 Fuc. check considers branches already used preceding pattern can describe several residues, Gal-(!Gal-GlcNAc-)Man. Keep attachment dash inside absence group, immediately ), write attachment residue directly . Bare !Fuc, [!Fuc], absence groups without final dash rejected. Unlike [^Fuc], matches includes one non-Fuc residue, (!Fuc-) checks condition adds residues match. Consequently, [^Fuc]-GlcNAc requires non-Fuc residue GlcNAc; (!Fuc-)GlcNAc can match GlcNAc alone Fuc branch.

title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: Use square brackets (?:...) group path. Ordinary parentheses mean branch, path group. Attach repetition operator group: [Gal]?: zero one Gal. [Gal]*: zero consecutive Gal residues. [Gal]+: one consecutive Gal residues. [Gal]{2}: exactly two consecutive Gal residues. [Gal]{2,4}: two four consecutive Gal residues. [Gal]{2,}: least two consecutive Gal residues. [Gal]{,4}: zero four consecutive Gal residues. group can contain one residue: [Galb4-GlcNAcb3]{2} repeats two-residue path twice. Use grouped syntax repetition rather forms Gal*, rejected. Repetition greedy default: longer repetitions tried first. Append ? try shorter repetitions first, [Gal]+?. either case, rest pattern must also match. Open upper bounds limited input graph, fixed repeat count. pattern permits zero repetitions never produces empty match.

title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: Assertions restrict match allowed without adding residues: ^Gal requires Gal non-reducing terminus (residue residues attached non-reducing side). GlcNAc$ requires GlcNAc reducing end. Gal% requires Gal internal: neither non-reducing terminus reducing-end residue. Lookaround checks neighbouring path without including result. Lookahead examines reducing-end direction: Gal-(?=GlcNAc) matches Gal next residue GlcNAc, whereas Gal-(?!GlcNAc) requires next residue match GlcNAc (absent). Lookbehind examines non-reducing direction: (?<=Gal-)GlcNAc matches GlcNAc Gal attached , (?<!Gal-)GlcNAc requires Gal path exists. Paths inside lookbehind still written towards reducing end, just like rest pattern. Negative lookbehind branch absence equivalent start pattern: (?<!Gal-)GlcNAc (!Gal-)GlcNAc match GlcNAc directly attached Gal non-reducing side, regardless linkage. Neither assertion adds residues match. preceding path, two assertions differ. Negative lookbehind checks attached paths, including residues already matched, whereas branch absence checks paths already used preceding pattern. example, Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc, Gal-(!Gal-)GlcNAc matches additional Gal branch. Gal-(?<!Gal-)GlcNAc match already matched Gal still counts negative lookbehind. Lookaround, branch-absence checks, anchors repeated. Assertions alone produce match every returned match must contain least one residue.

title: Compile a Glycan Regular Expression — rex_compile
text: Use (?<name>...) give matched path name. example, (?<terminal>Gal)-GlcNAc matches two-residue path captures Gal terminal. rex_match() rex_match_all() return full match match column captured fragments named columns. named-capture syntax extension glycowork. Capture names must start letter, contain letters, digits, underscores, unique within pattern. name match reserved. Use (?:...) grouping without named capture desired. See rex_detect() matches ordered counted, including overlapping matches matches contained within larger ones.

title: Query Glycan Structures with Regular Expressions — rex_query
text: matching unit connected structural trace. glycowork, first successful trace per starting node retained, strict subsets traces removed. Distinct branches equal sequences remain distinct matches. title: glyrex 0.0.0.9000
text: Query functions now use glycans instead string automatically parse formats supported glyparse::auto_parse(), including mixed-format vectors. Branch absence requires (!branch-); bare !linked-residue groups missing final attachment dash rejected. [^] always consumes nonmatching residue, including linkage constraint. Residue negation uses [^]; [!] spelling rejected migration guidance. (!...-) always asserts branch absence: (!Fuc-) forbids Fuc branch attachment residue, (!Fuca3-) restricts forbidden branch alpha1-3 linkage. rex_compile() compiles glycowork-style glycan patterns branches, repetition, location anchors, lookaround, named captures, including glyrepr reducing-end configuration constraints. rex_detect(), rex_count(), rex_extract(), rex_extract_all(), rex_match(), rex_match_all(), rex_locate(), rex_locate_all(), rex_subset(), rex_which() provide stringr-style structural queries IUPAC strings glyrepr structures. Queries reject glycans floating parts floating substituents.
